# Lab 5 — CI/CD & GitOps

## Task 1 — CI Pipeline and ArgoCD Setup

### 5.1 CI workflow

The repository contains a GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The workflow runs on pushes to `main`, builds Docker images for the Gateway, Events, and Payments services, logs in to GitHub Container Registry, and pushes the images to `ghcr.io` using the commit SHA as the image tag.

GitHub Actions run evidence:

<img alt="GitHub Actions CI workflow completed successfully" src="data:image/png;base64,
" />

### 5.2 Container images in GitHub Container Registry

The GitHub Packages page shows the three QuickTicket container images published to GitHub Container Registry:

- `quickticket-gateway`
- `quickticket-payments`
- `quickticket-events`

<img alt="GitHub Packages page showing the three QuickTicket container images" src="data:image/png;base64,
" />

### 5.3 Kubernetes manifests updated for registry images

The Kubernetes manifests were updated to use images from GitHub Container Registry instead of local k3d images. The application images use `ghcr.io/rmcavalcante7/quickticket-*` references, `imagePullPolicy: Always`, and the `ghcr-secret` image pull secret so Kubernetes can pull the images from GHCR.

### 5.4 ArgoCD installed

ArgoCD was installed in the `argocd` namespace and accessed through a local port-forward to `https://localhost:8443`.

### 5.5 ArgoCD Application created

The `quickticket` ArgoCD Application was created with:

```text
Repository: https://github.com/rmcavalcante7/SRE-Intro.git
Path: k8s
Destination server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
Destination namespace: default
Sync policy: Automated
```

### 5.6 GitOps loop verification

A visible change was committed to Git by adding the label `version: "v2"` to the Gateway Pod template labels in `k8s/gateway.yaml`. After pushing the change and synchronizing ArgoCD, the label was visible in the live Kubernetes Deployment.

Command:

```bash
kubectl get deployment gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.metadata.labels.version}'; echo
```

Output:

```text
v2
```

Evidence of the synchronized label:

<img alt="kubectl output showing gateway Deployment template label version v2" src="data:image/png;base64,
" />

### 5.7 Proof of Work answer

If someone manually runs `kubectl edit` on a Kubernetes resource managed by ArgoCD, the live cluster state can become different from the desired state stored in Git. ArgoCD detects this difference as drift and marks the application or resource as `OutOfSync`.

The manual edit should not be treated as the source of truth. The desired state remains the manifest version stored in Git. When ArgoCD synchronizes the application, it reconciles the resource back to the Git-defined state. If automatic self-healing is enabled, ArgoCD can revert the manual change automatically; otherwise, the drift remains visible until a sync operation reconciles it.
